VP insight: The four cards above show the cohort-level starting exposure, remaining exposure, burn-down and burn-down %. The primary table ties those insights directly to the 19 approved Feature Value risks. Burn-down is a reduction indicator against the fixed 16-Aug >240-day cohort; new >240-day inflow is excluded. Changes can reflect consumption, site balance, returns, reclassification or other inventory movements.
Aging >180 Days — Management Guardrails
Aging >180 Days %Suggested interpretation
< 3%🟢 Excellent
3–5%🟢 Healthy / best-in-class territory
5–8%🟡 Watch
8–10%🟠 High
10–15%🔴 Problematic
>15%🔴 Critical / strong E&O risk
Footnote: These thresholds are management guardrails, not an audited laptop-industry benchmark. They are proposed considering the high obsolescence exposure of laptop inventory and the broader PC/electronics industry. Aging >180 days is a risk indicator and should not, by itself, be interpreted as an E&O classification.
PM Recommendations
make the weekly tracker the system of record, codify decision rules, and run a predictable weekly governance cadence.
● Recommended operating model
Executive recommendation

Do not create another report. Formalize the existing weekly EO tracker as the single source of truth, turn repeated case-by-case decisions into explicit IF/THEN rules, and use a fixed Mon–Fri cadence with measurable escalation triggers. The goal is to move from repeated discussion to committed action and measurable burn-down.

1

One Source of Truth

Use the weekly EO tracker as the official record. Map GSM, Procurement, Demand Planning, Inventory Planning and Finance inputs; reconcile discrepancies before publishing; assign a single accountable owner per field; obtain written sign-off.

2

Rules Over Judgment

Convert recurring decisions into testable rules. Example: Site Balance only when the destination has backlog or confirmed demand. LTB follows the agreed Hold / Partial Broker path. Exceptions should route to human review.

3

Weekly Governance Cadence

Run a fixed Analyze → Align → Action → Track cadence, feeding the Friday finance readout. Measure committed dates, date adherence and $ mitigated—not just inventory aging.

Decision rules to operationalize

These are the recurring decision patterns identified in the meeting-derived framework and should be captured as version-controlled business rules.
ScenarioRecommended ruleEscalate whenDashboard implication
Site BalanceEligible only when destination has backlog or confirmed demand / committed consumption.Destination signal is missing or disputed.Flag as exception rather than auto-recommending transfer.
LTBUse the agreed Hold or Partial Broker path; validate lifecycle / EOL and consumption profile.Demand is insufficient, EOL timing changes, or broker economics require approval.Show action, target date and expected mitigation separately from aging.
ConsumeKeep when forecast / demand supports depletion within the agreed horizon and FIFO consumption is feasible.Forecast deteriorates or aged exposure remains flat for two cycles.Show burn-down against the fixed cohort.
Broker / E&OUse when qualification / demand recovery is not viable and brokerage creates a positive recovery path.Approval is pending beyond the committed date or economics become unattractive.Track $ accrual, broker impact and mitigation independently.
Data anomalyStop publication of the affected KPI until the source discrepancy is reconciled.Bucket totals, plant mapping or MOS math do not reconcile.Surface a data-quality flag before leadership review.

Weekly governance cadence

Fixed ownership and outputs replace reactive / late-stage escalation.
StageDayOwnerOutput
AnalyzeMon–TueBronson / KarthikRefresh data, run rules, flag anomalies and data-quality issues.
AlignWedCategory / Procurement / Demand PlanningConfirm or dispute proposed actions and commit real target dates—not placeholder “In Progress”.
ActionThuIndividual action ownersExecute actions and update status on assigned lines.
TrackFriBronsonConsolidate tracker + one-slide summary and feed the Friday readout.

Meeting adjustments reflected in this view

The framework emphasizes business rules first, fewer competing reports, action accountability, and escalation when actions stall.

Business rules first

Build and validate the decision logic before attempting system automation; use the current 19-FV cohort as the pilot set.

Action over repetition

Replace repeated discussion with visible owners, target dates, weekly updates and a defined escalation path.

Control the data

Reconcile plant mapping, MOS and bucket math before leadership consumption; version-control threshold and rule changes.
